title: VCC administration
blurb: Clients, permissions, skills, prompts, DNC, and the PCs that drop calls.
summary: The administrator console is where the domain becomes a floor people can work.

lessons.title: Two administrator applications
paragraphs: The technical requirements still describe a Java VCC Administrator and a web Administrator Console. Java is not supported on Mac workstations with ARM processors. On those machines the document says to use VCC Administrator via Web in Admin Console.

Because web applications do not need a Java SE subscription, the same document strongly recommends moving to the Five9 Plus applications. The Java client is still documented, with named JRE 8 update builds. Treat that list as dated and re-read the PDF before you image a PC.

lessons.title: User profiles before user accounts
objectives: Keep admin rights off the agent profile
paragraphs: The planning roadmap says to define user profiles before you add user accounts. A profile is the permission bundle. An account is the person. Creating people first and hoping the default permissions match the job is how reporting and call-variable edits go missing.
Skill groups then take users who already have the agent or supervisor role. An administrator account is not automatically a member of a queue.

lessons.title: Skill groups are the queues
objectives: Put one agent in two groups
paragraphs: Skill groups organize agent and supervisor users into the queues that belong to campaigns. A user can be in several groups. A campaign can list several groups.

The same help topic uses two different places for the assignment. Outbound campaigns take skills on the Skills tab. Inbound and autodial campaigns take them on a tab named Outbound Skills. Read that name twice before you decide the tab is missing.

lessons.title: Prompts before the script
paragraphs: The inbound and autodial roadmaps tell you to define and record prompts before you build the IVR. A Play or Menu module can only speak what the prompt library already holds, or what a text-to-speech entry supplies in that module.
Skill groups have their own audio: voicemail greetings and other skill audio. A campaign prompt and a skill greeting are different objects. Replacing one does not replace the other.

lessons.title: Do-not-call is a list, and a module
objectives: Do not confuse it with a disposition label
paragraphs: Outbound product material lists DNC list management with time-zone rules and Certified Caller as compliance tools. Inside the IVR, Set DNC is a real module in the modules chapter. A spoken 'remove me' path should hit that module, not a note in a disposition comment.
A disposition called DNC is not the same object as the Set DNC module. Use both only if you know which system each one updates. This lab does not pretend they are automatically the same switch.
uncertain: Public pages do not spell out, in one paragraph, whether a custom disposition named DNC writes the same list as the Set DNC module. Confirm in your domain.

lessons.title: Workstations that drop live calls
objectives: Quote the bandwidth table, not a guess
paragraphs: The technical requirements tell you to turn off Windows 11 Efficiency Mode on PCs that take live calls. Efficiency Mode can limit CPU and sleep inactive tabs, and the PDF says that can drop active Five9 calls. If you leave it on, use a high-performance power plan.

Headsets should be USB with noise canceling. Analog headsets are not supported. Wireless is discouraged when more than 10 agents are active, because of delay and quality. Wired LAN is recommended. Wi-Fi is allowed only if each user still meets the bandwidth numbers. Satellite and cellular, including 5G, are not supported.

lessons.title: Reason codes, voicemail, and what admin is not
objectives: Treat voicemail as a skill object
Keep dialer math in the campaign
paragraphs: Not every silence is a carrier failure. Agents have Not Ready states. TCPA manual touch even forces Not Ready when preview time expires. Skill groups can hold voicemail, greetings, and messages. Those are administrator objects with their own reports.

Admin work does not include inventing a dialer ratio in a spreadsheet and calling it the Five9 algorithm. The dialer has documented modes and a documented abandon window. Configuration belongs in the campaign, not in a side file.
